content.value: Evaluate relational and equality expressions; distinguish inclusive boundaries, assignment, primitive equality, and reference identity.

A boolean expression evaluates to true or false. Numeric comparisons use <, <=, >, and >=. Equality and inequality use == and !=. Select the operator that matches the specification: “at least” includes equality, while “greater than” excludes it. Arithmetic expressions can appear on either side of a comparison.

For primitive numbers, == compares their values. For reference variables, == checks whether they identify the same object, including the case where both are null. A class’s equals method can define content equality; use String.equals when comparing text. The single equals sign assigns rather than comparing.
eligible is true and above is false. first == second is false because the constructor calls create different objects. first.equals(second) is true because the character sequences match.
A quoted "true" is a String, not a boolean literal. Do not use == as a general test of String contents. Test exact boundary values because replacing >= with > changes behavior at equality.
